title: DCP Noisy Cascaded Dyadic Bit-Peeling vs. Unpruned CNOT Tree Sample Complexity Bridge
claims: Under independent Z-dephasing gamma_0 in (0, 1), minimum-weight adaptive syndrome pruning reduces level-ell bit-peeling sample overhead from doubly-exponential gamma_0^{-2^ell} to singly-exponential O((32/9)^ell * gamma_0^{-4}).
At gamma_0 = 1.0, cumulative raw-qubit cost across t levels is 2^t - 1; at gamma_0 = 0.85, adaptive pruning reduces cumulative sample cost by >35x at t=5 and >4800x at t=6 (>8100x at level ell=6).
